files.Title: AAComm.CommAPI
files.Summary:
An API for handling communication with the AACommServer executable.


The API provides low-level send/receive capabilities + special functionality.


All *synchronous* functions are mutually-locking, and should not be called from multiple threads


Proper work-flow: (see usage details at every function description)


0. subscribe to events: Long operations: <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.OnLongOperationStarted" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> / <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.OnLongOperationEnded" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>, General Error: <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.OnCommsError" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>, Push: <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.OnPushMessageReceived" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (TBD)


1. <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.StartAACommServer(System.String)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref><p></p>

2. <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.TestConnection(AAComm.Services.ConnectionData%2cSystem.Boolean)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (not mandatory, can be used to determine <xref href="AAComm.Services.ConnectionData.ControllerType" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>)


3. <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.Connect(AAComm.Services.ConnectionData%2cSystem.Boolean)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref><p></p>

4. <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.Send(AAComm.Services.AACommMessage)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and/or <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.SendReceive(AAComm.Services.AACommMessage)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (both safe from any thread, in any combination — independent FIFO pipelines for ordinary messages)


5. <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.Disconnect" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref><p></p>

6. <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.CloseAACommServer(System.Boolean)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> (not mandatory)

files.Title: AAComm.Services.AACommMessage
files.Summary:
This class describes the message sent to AAComm <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.Send(AAComm.Services.AACommMessage)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and <xref href="AAComm.CommAPI.SendReceive(AAComm.Services.AACommMessage)" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> methods


Two CTOR sets are available: for the synchronous SendReceive() function, and the asynchronous Send() function


Every CTOR set has 2 "sub-types" regarding <xref href="AAComm.Services.AACommMessage.MessageType" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and <xref href="AAComm.Services.AACommMessage.TimeoutMs" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref><p></p>

The 'implicit' CTOR resolves these parameters automatically from the <xref href="AAComm.Services.AACommMessage.Message" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> argument


The 'explicit' CTOR expects the user to specify these arguments. For expert use only.


To use the "Bulk Message" functionality: use the 'explicit' CTOR, set MessageType to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.MessageType.BulkMessage" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and Timeout to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.TimeoutMs.Default" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
To use the "Special CNCA Bulk Message" functionality: use the 'explicit' CTOR, set MessageType to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.MessageType.BulkMessageCNC" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and Timeout to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.TimeoutMs.Default" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
To use the "Special CNCB Bulk Message" functionality: use the 'explicit' CTOR, set MessageType to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.MessageType.BulkMessageCNCB" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and Timeout to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.TimeoutMs.Default" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
To use the "Special Bulk Message for CNCA" functionality: use the 'explicit' CTOR, set MessageType to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.MessageType.SpecialBulk" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and Timeout to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.TimeoutMs.Default" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>
To use the "Special Bulk Message for CNCB" functionality: use the 'explicit' CTOR, set MessageType to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.MessageType.SpecialBulkB" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref> and Timeout to <xref href="AAComm.Shared.TimeoutMs.Default" data-throw-if-not-resolved="false"></xref>

files.Title: AAComm.Services.Diagnostics.AACommDebugLog
files.Summary:
Process-wide, zero-config, always-on diagnostic log for the AAComm client — the client-side counterpart of AACommServer's debug log. Session-lifecycle events (construction, connect outcomes, sync-timeout expiries, FATALs, disconnects) accumulate in an in-memory ring; healthy steady state does zero file IO. A severe event (sync phase-2 teardown, FATAL, comms error) snapshots the ring to %LocalAppData%\PCSuite\AAComm_DebugLogs{yyyy_MM_dd_HH-mm-ss}{process}{pid}_{trigger}.log off the hot path (debounced, 5 s), because a library in the customer's process has no reliable exit hook to save on. Never per-message traffic — that is the AACommServer comm log's job.

Every line is tagged HH:mm:ss.fff [api#N/conn#M] text: api#N identifies the instance, conn#M its successive channel opens; the connect line carries the full endpoint (and the socket's local port, which AACommServer's log can join against its per-client UserId).

files.Title: AAComm.Services.PushData.AACommPushMsgBase
files.Summary:
Base type for controller push messages.

Expected raw message format:

[VERSION_PUSH].[SOURCE],[VERSION_DATA].[DATA]

Where:

  • VERSION_PUSH: integer protocol version for the overall push feature
  • SOURCE: integer enum value () telling which derived message type to create
  • VERSION_DATA: integer version for the payload format
  • DATA: raw payload (may be ASCII string or raw binary bytes depending on SOURCE/VERSION_DATA)

files.Title: AAComm.Services.PushData.AACommPushMsgError
files.Summary: Error/fallback push message type. Created when parsing or constructing a derived type fails. Holds the original raw bytes and the exception for logging/debugging.

files.Title: AAComm.Services.PushData.AACommPushMsgUP
files.Summary:
SOURCE == 1 (User Program):

For VERSION_DATA = 1, the DATA section contains raw binary data (little-endian) with multiple printf messages.

Binary packet structure (after the header, before the messages slots):

  • uint8 n: number of printf messages
  • uint16 missed: messages dropped since last flush
  • uint16 freeBytesMsgQueue: remaining free bytes in FW printf buffer
  • uint8 freeDescSlots: remaining free descriptor slots

Then n times:

  • uint32 timeSec: seconds since power-on
  • uint32 timeTick: sub-second tick
  • uint8 thread: thread ID
  • uint16 len: text length in bytes
  • byte[len] textBytes: raw ASCII text (NOT null-terminated)

 7   (6): PosRef, VelRef, CurrRef, dPosRef, CNCAPosRef, CNCAdPosRef
 8   (7): LockEn, LockCntr, LockVal, EventOn, EventCntr, EventNextPos, EventSelect
 9   (5): UserParam_1..5
10   (2): DInPortHigh, BoardTemp
Please refer to the user manual for more information.
